title: Align: The MyFitnessPal Story
coreMove: Use linked priorities to make cross-team execution visible before local work pulls apart.
sourcePressure: MyFitnessPal is the company case for alignment, with support only for connected priorities, dependency visibility, and silo drift.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not invent MyFitnessPal internal product detail, metrics, or management biography.

sourceAnchors.name: MyFitnessPal
sourceAnchors.detail: The source stabilizes MyFitnessPal as the company case for alignment, without authorizing invented internal scenes or metrics.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: MyFitnessPal should land as a named alignment case, where visible priorities keep teams from optimizing separate corners of the same product.

hook: A team discovers OKRs in a conference room and suddenly gets aligned
A dashboard glows on a Monday morning and reveals the truth
A leader writes a goal on a whiteboard and everyone understands
opening with Align: The MyFitnessPal Story as a definition rather than a pressure
counterintuition: Measurement is not bureaucracy, it is clarity
Goals are not dreams, they are systems
Accountability is not punishment, it is ownership
MyFitnessPal is not a mindset, it is a system
tryThisNow: Set a timer and write three goals
Ask yourself what matters most right now
write one OKR without checking whether it changes behavior
examples: generic startup roadmap meeting with sticky notes
home chore chart with vague family goals
student group in a classroom choosing priorities
team lead reviewing a color-coded dashboard

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.stakes: one label change can fail if teams see only their local tasks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia links the packaging objective to support scripts and quality signoff before any lane can claim done

exampleSpecs.stakes: members will blame the studio if back-end and front-room work drift apart
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Etienne makes billing cutover, coach messaging, and desk training visible on one alignment board

exampleSpecs.stakes: the app can ship while station staff remain unready

exampleSpecs.stakes: applicants see one portal but offices carry separate definitions of readiness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Maja turns three local launch lists into one visible applicant journey with dependency owners

skillTargets: detect silo drift behind local success

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one cross-team launch and write the one shared readiness line that every team must be able to see.
